video.title: Are You Sleeping on the Atlanta Hawks? [BEST Hawks Outlook]

summary: Josh Lloyd and Brad Rowland (Locked On Hawks) preview the 2026-27 Atlanta Hawks, the first full season after the Trae Young era. Brad thinks the roster is a bit better than at the end of last season. They added Lu Dort, Aaron Wiggins, Kingston Flemings, Devin Carter and Ryan Nembhard, and still have two roster spots too many to clear. The likely starters are CJ McCollum, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu. Alexander-Walker should regress toward his pre-All-Star level. Jalen Johnson probably wore down but should match last season's production. Okongwu is finally the clear starting center: a stretch big whose blocks and offensive rebounds dropped while his threes, assists and steals rose. Brad predicts 46 wins and a spot somewhere between fourth and eighth in the East.

rules.text: This season the East is stronger and fewer bottom teams are tanking, so a team can get better and still win fewer games. Do not read fewer wins as a worse team.
rules.quote: you can be a better team and win fewer games and that's okay as long as we're just understanding

rules.text: When a player has an extreme hot stretch, such as a post All-Star run, use the earlier part of his season as the baseline and expect the shooting to come down.
rules.quote: So there's going to be a bit of usage and ball handling changes plus that insane shooting is going to come down.

rules.text: To judge a player's production and minutes, look at who was around him, who was out, and how he gets used when the team is healthy. Big games that came while a teammate was out may not carry over.
rules.quote: who was around, who wasn't around, and how were they used and how do they get used when the team looks whole?

rules.text: Players who go for more blocks commit more fouls. As players age and their minutes go up, their block and foul rates tend to drop. Starters playing big minutes cannot risk foul trouble.
rules.quote: when you go for more blocks, you commit more fouls. And when you're every player, like as they get older, block rate down

rules.text: A center who takes more threes plays farther from the rim. His offensive rebounds and rim finishing tend to drop, while assists and three-point attempts go up.
rules.quote: when you're out there taking more threes, you're in a different position. So you're working not exactly under the rim.

player_notes.text: Expect regression after his extreme post All-Star shooting run. Brad uses his pre All-Star numbers (about 20 points, 58% true shooting) as the baseline, which is still very good.
player_notes.quote: Alexander Walker is like my baseline level, which is still really good. You know, 20 points a game

player_notes.text: Sneaky key player. If his inside finishing returns to past levels, he could score 18 to 19 points per game instead of 15, with efficiency that helps in fantasy.

player_notes.text: Has always had very good hands and good feel. He handles the ball better than most centers.
